evidence_scope: Publisher article pages, abstracts, highlights and available introduction/section previews. No claim that inaccessible full texts were completely reviewed.

sources.title: Don't forget flexibility contracts when redesigning short-term electricity markets
sources.verified_metadata: Energy Economics 151, 108980, November 2025; five named authors
sources.used_claim: Complete bilateral flexibility contracts in sequential clearing can deliver look-ahead benefits comparable to integrated dispatch.
sources.not_claimed: No claim that the paper contains no bounds or no duality; the distinction concerns the economic object and common-service counterfactual.

sources.title: The price of flexibility in electricity markets
sources.verified_metadata: Energy Economics 150, 108769, October 2025; Subhojit Biswas, Bahar Çavdar, Alfredo Garcia, Joseph Geunes
sources.used_claim: A two-settlement strategic model links persistent day-ahead premiums to flexibility, disruption risk and constrained arbitrage.
sources.not_claimed: No inference that a market equilibrium premium directly identifies our fixed-path contract-rights increment.

sources.title: Energy flexibility procurement strategy in competitive demand response markets: Dual-channel supply chain perspective
sources.verified_metadata: Xinyue Fei, Cheng Lyu, Yibo Ding; Energy Economics 161, 109542, 2026; publisher online date 5 August, institutional issue date September
sources.used_claim: Dual-channel demand-response procurement is modelled as strategic interaction; direct procurement can reduce double marginalisation.
sources.not_claimed: No use of the paper's case-study percentages as calibration for the present computing workload.

novelty_boundary: The contrast is an inference from the explicitly defined economic objects, not an exhaustive priority claim. The paper contributes a controller-independent, service-matched, account-matched monetary enclosure and exclusion comparison; it does not invent weak duality or a new equilibrium-pricing theory.
